accuracy.evidence: Every number was recomputed: 2x² + 5x − 3 = 0 gives (−5 ± 7) ÷ 4 = 0.5 or −3; x² − 6x + 5 has discriminant 36 − 20 = 16; x² + 4x + 1 gives (−4 ± √12) ÷ 2 = −0.27 or −3.73; x² − 2x − 8 gives 4 and −2; x² + 2x − 4 has roots −1 ± √5 ≈ 1.24 and −3.24; y = x² − 2x + c has discriminant 4 − 4c, zero at c = 1. The formula derivation by completing the square, the three discriminant cases and the repeated root at −b/2a match the DfE GCSE subject content (A18) and CCSS HSA-REI.B.4b. Practice p4 is built from chosen integer roots so every parameter corner gives an exact answer.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented GCSE examiner-report slips: signs dropped when reading b and c and reading before rearranging (step 1 options for 3x² + 4 = 8x and 5 − x² + 2x = 0, challenge 'rearr', m2), −b sign (step 3 stage 1, slip 1, challenge 'sign'), b² taken as negative (step 3 prediction, slip 2, challenge 'sq', m1), dividing only the root by 2a (step 3 stage 5, slip 3, challenge 'half', m5), losing the ± root (slip 4, m8), adding 4ac (stage 4 option 7), and treating a negative discriminant as a negative root (step 2 prediction, challenge 'neg').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagqform is about the formula's own mechanics: choosing the a, b, c triple from rearranged layouts, a draggable y = x² − 2x + c whose live b² − 4ac readout and root dots switch between 2, 1 and 0, a five-stage evaluation where each stage has the classic wrong value, an x-axis marker for irrational roots checked against −1 ± √5, and find-the-wrong-line workings. flagcsq builds completing the square with algebra tiles; flagsqroot and flagzprod solve by square roots and factorising. Similarity gate passed under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner meets each rule by acting: dragging the curve up shows the root dots merge at b² − 4ac = 0 and vanish when it goes negative; picking −25 for b² is refused with (−5) × (−5) = 25; choosing 5.5 or 4.5 is refused because only the root was halved; marking a point where y is not 0 reports whether the curve is above or below the axis. Each success line restates the rule (rearrange to = 0, divide the whole top by 2a).

predictions.evidence: Three predictions each have a tempting wrong answer the lab disproves: b = 3 in 2x² − 3x − 5 (step 1, disproved by the sign feedback), a negative discriminant gives one negative root (step 2, disproved when the curve lifts off the axis and the dots disappear), and b² = −25 when b = −5 (step 3, disproved by the stage feedback).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Each wrong challenge answer gets a message naming the slip: 'sign' (−b not flipped), 'coef' (used c for b), 'sq' and 'dbl' (b² negative or 2b), 'neg' (negative discriminant), 'zero' (repeated root counted as two or none), 'rearr' (c read before rearranging), 'half' (2a under the root only). Six questions rotate on retry.

readability.evidence: Learner text is FK grade 2.9 against the 6.5 target: short sentences, one term (discriminant) defined where it first appears, and the stages listed in order. Adult text is FK 8.8 against 9.5 and names the specification codes and terms coefficient, discriminant, repeated root, irrational. Lab prompts are one line (Stage 1 of 5: −b = ?).

no_filler.evidence: Every learner paragraph does one job: why the formula, rearranging and reading a, b, c, the discriminant cases, then the stages and sign traps. No banned phrases and explanation overlap is under 12%. Lab feedback lines give the exact arithmetic, for example '(−5)² = (−5) × (−5) = +25. A square is never negative.'

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots in dark and light for all six steps: the three a, b, c rows are full-width 50 px targets, the parabola graphs use the full width with axis labels readable, the discriminant chip shrinks to fit and now shows 4 − 4 × (−2) with brackets, stage options are three equal tiles, and the root step has 0.5 and 0.05 nudge buttons plus 'Is this a root?' under the canvas. Nothing clipped.

accessibility.evidence: The walkthrough gate completed every task with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found no violations in either theme. Every drag has a button route (Curve up or down by 0.5, marker nudges and 'Is this a root?', Line 1 to 3 with the line text in the label), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten with the discriminant value and root count after every move.
